Pizza Tower was a manic, insane thrill ride throughout. The graphics and soundtrack are a treat to the eyes and ears despite the fast paced nature of the game. Every level has something unique to offer and very rarely are gimmicks repeated, giving each level their own identity. My first play through was delightful, yet in some parts stressful given the pizza time segments. However when going after the elusive P-Ranks, it becomes a whole different beast. The stress is cranked up to 11 now that you need to find all 3 secrets, Jerome the janitor with the level's secret item, maintain a high score and your current combo AND play through the pizza time segment twice. Not all levels are created equal in this department (namely Gnome Forest and Pizzascare) but all of them were satisfying to complete when all was said and done. My favorites were easily Deep Dish 9, Don't Make a Sound, and especially War. Platforming fanatics shouldn't miss out on this game, but only go after 101% completion at your own risk.

Well, simply put, this is an art of a platformer. I'm almost certain you've seen or at least heard some of the other reviews here talking about how this game is inspired by the Wario games and how "It's so nostalgic!" (*Some* of them are like Persona fans in the way that they have never played a single game from the series) but it's true on the nostalgic part in many ways even for someone like me who never touched a Wario game. This game reminds me of Pizza Hut from the 90's along with some 90's ads that you'd see in the NBA or NFL from WAY before my time and the game can be nostalgic in your own method too, in such a way that has so many variables and options of memories/nostalgic moments to choose to the point where t's almost poetic how it's really similar to a customizable pizza from a buffet like CiCi's Pizza or some other place.

And if you're not here for nostalgia, that's fine too since this game offers a classic Nintendo vibe for platforming but actually done way better.

A game with lots of charm and fun absurdity, heavily inspired by the old Warioland games.

The artstyle is really catching and the OST was ridiculously good, likely the reason you even considered buying this game.

The game is fluid and works well overall, completing the game isnt hard, but 100% WILL require you put some real effort, since it essentially requires you to flawless it, learning all the moves of your arsenal, every secret, every enemy position, etc, and with bosses learning how to defeat them without taking dmg.

And regarding bosses, they're good, each one brings their own flare and are fun to face, and like mentioned before, the ost is awesome for these guys.

Regarding how the levels work, you essentially play it has a platformer where you wanna keep your combo going, the bigger the combo the more points you get, which will earn you a rank at the end of the level, but before that, once you reach the end of the level, you gotta do "It's Pizza Time" which requires you to run all the way back to the start of the level on a timer, and once you complete it, you unlock the second lap, which requires you to do the runback a second time with the remaining time in order to earn the max rank.

Overall, it was a fun game that i definitely recommend, but like mentioned early, for those looking for completion, youre in for a world of pain.

Without a doubt one of my favourite games of all time,it's perfect for any platformer addicts. The pacing is amazing,the game is addicting and the moveset for both Peppino and Noise are both fun. For example, Peppino is mainly about speed meanwhile Noise has a wacky playstyle, giving the players a variety of ways to play. Gustavo and Brick are slow yet somewhat fun to play as, yet they are only playable in Gnome Forest and Pig City.

Overall,this game is one of the greatest indie games and i would highly recommend it. However, I wouldn't recommend it to people who do not like fast-paced games or if you're new to platforming.
